title: Representation Entanglement for Generation: Training Diffusion Transformers

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Abstract states: 'SiT-L/2 + REG trained for 400K iterations achieves comparable FID scores to SiT-XL/2 + REPA trained for 4M iterations,' whereas the Introduction states: 'SiT-L/2 + REPA trained for 400K iterations achieves performance comparable to SiT-XL/2 + REPA trained for 4M iterations (see Tab. 1).' These two statements name different methods (REG vs. REPA) for the same claim. Using Table 1's own REPA numbers (SiT-L/2+REPA@400K=9.7 vs SiT-XL/2+REPA@4M=5.9) the two are not 'comparable' (a 3.8-point gap), so the Introduction's version (using REPA) is both internally contradictory with the Abstract and not supported by Table 1.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 vs. Table 9 (Appendix C) and Table 4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 1 and Table 9 both claim to report SiT+REG results on ImageNet 256x256 'without CFG', yet they give substantially different FID values for identical configurations: SiT-B/2+REG@400K is 21.8 in Table 1 but 15.2 in Table 9 (also 15.22 in Tables 3/5); SiT-L/2+REG@100K/400K is 17.2/9.8 in Table 1 but 11.4/4.6 in Table 9; SiT-XL/2+REG@200K/400K/1M/2.4M/4M is 7.1/5.6/4.3/3.8/3.3 in Table 1 but 5.0/3.4/2.7/2.2/1.8 in Table 9. Table 4's reported REG numbers at 400K (FID 3.44, IS 184.13) match Table 9, not Table 1, further confirming the inconsistency between tables describing the same experiment.

The text claims 'SiT-B/2 + REG outperforms SiT-B/2 + REPA by 9.2 FID points' but Table 1 shows REPA=24.4 and REG=21.8 (difference 2.6, not 9.2). It also claims REG(B/2) 'surpasses SiT-L/2 trained for 400K iterations by 3.6 points', but Table 1 shows SiT-L/2 baseline FID=18.8 while REG(B/2)=21.8, meaning REG is actually worse, not better, contradicting the claim regardless of which number is used. Later, the text states 'SiT-L/2 + REG achieves an FID of 4.6 at 400K steps...' though Table 1 lists 9.8 for that cell, and 'At 4M steps, REG achieves a record-low FID of 1.8,' though Table 1 lists 3.3 for SiT-XL/2+REG at 4M. These numbers instead match Table 9, not the cited Table 1.

The text states 'class token entanglement alone consistently enhances generation quality, with FID improvements ranging from 0.95 to 6.33 points' and 'DINOv2-B delivers optimal performance, achieving a 19.18% FID reduction and 35.86% IS improvement compared to the SiT-B/2 baseline.' However, Table 6 shows SiT-B/2 baseline FID=33.0, IS=43.70, and DINOv2-B entangled FID=29.9, IS=52.3 — an FID improvement of only 3.1 points (9.39% reduction) and an IS improvement of 8.6 (19.68%), with the full range of FID improvements across all variants being 1.2 to 3.1 points (CLIP-L: 33.0→31.8=1.2; DINOv2-L: 33.0→30.0=3.0; DINOv2-B: 33.0→29.9=3.1). None of these figures match the stated 0.95–6.33 range, 19.18%, or 35.86%.

Both tables purport to report SiT-XL/2+REG results on ImageNet 256x256 with CFG using the same guidance interval, yet the values differ at matching epoch counts: at 80 epochs, Table 2 reports FID 2.15/IS 280.1 while Table 8 reports FID 1.86/IS 321.4; at 160 epochs, Table 2 reports FID 1.75/IS 290.5 while Table 8 reports FID 1.59/IS 304.6; at 480 epochs, Table 2 reports FID 1.38/IS 297.0 while Table 8 reports FID 1.40/IS 296.9; at 800 epochs, Table 2 reports FID 1.34/IS 300.4 while Table 8 reports FID 1.36/IS 299.4. These are inconsistent duplicate reportings of ostensibly the same experiment.

The text states: 'All metrics report the average and standard deviation over three independent runs with different random seeds. The results indicate consistent trends where REG achieves lower mean FID scores while reducing variance compared to baselines.' However, Table 1 lists only single-point FID values for each configuration with no mean±std or variance reported anywhere in the table, so the claim about averaging over three seeds and reduced variance is unsupported by the presented data.

predicted_errors.error_location: Eq. (9) and surrounding text in Section 3.2
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text defines alignment at 'specific transformer layers n' (n=4 or n=8) and states h_phi(h_t^[n]) ∈ R^{(N+1)×D_vf} aligns with y_* ∈ R^{(N+1)×D_vf} (the concatenation of cls_* and f_*, i.e., N+1 tokens). However, Eq. (9) writes the loss as (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^{N} sim(y_*, h_φ(h_t^[n])), reusing the symbol 'n' simultaneously as the fixed layer index and as a summation index running only to N (not N+1), which both overloads notation and omits the class-token term from the stated (N+1)-token alignment, making the equation inconsistent with its own stated dimensionality.
